title.narrative: Protection, shelter and site coordination interventions addressing the impact of heightened hostilities in Lebanon, with a focus on providing critical support and information to displaced populations

description.narrative: Amidst increasing hostilities, the proposed project aims to provide comprehensive support to vulnerable groups in Lebanon affected by the escalation of cross-border clashes, including refugees.• The project seeks to ensure that accurate and up-to-date data on the needs of the displaced is collected through systematic protection monitoring. By conducting regular interviews and assessments, the UNHCR can identify specific needs related to all aspects of the displaced people’s lives including protection, shelter, food, healthcare and education. This is to allow UNHCR and partners to understand the specific needs and vulnerabilities of the displaced population and to respond swiftly to emerging needs. • UNHCR will ensure accountability to affected populations by broadening the audience of its existing communication channels, information repositories, and two-way complaint and feedback mechanisms to include both refugee communities and other newly displaced populations (including Lebanese IDPs), ensuring that communities across populations equally informed, are able to share their concerns and suggestions, and can be counselled or referred to relevant services. • The cash-for-shelter assistance will be provided as a one-off grant to support vulnerable refugees and Lebanese communities who have been displaced and are hosted or renting temporary shelters in addressing essential shelter needs in their accommodations. This assistance will cover minor shelter repairs and the payment of critical utility bills, such as water and electricity, to ensure basic living conditions are maintained.• Moreover, UNHCR will directly rehabilitate and repair collective shelters to enhance living conditions. Partitioning of spaces will increase the hosting capacity and provide safe and private spaces for women and girls. Repairs will focus on common spaces, windows, doors, electrical connections as well as water and sanitation facilities. Lighting fixtures, solar panels and water heaters will be installed where applicable. In addition, shelters will be adapted to also serve persons with disabilities. • In terms of site coordination and site management, UNHCR will ensure existing and newly identified sites to host displaced populations are adequately assessed, essential infrastructure provided, and the shelters managed in a structured manner. This will be done in close cooperation with other humanitarian agencies and local authorities. UNHCR will ensure general protection services are available specifically gender-based violence (GBV) and child protection services are integrated across all sites and coordinate with partners to ensure adequate access to clean water, sanitation, and hygiene kits for all displaced populations. The agency will continue to advocate for access of non-Lebanese populations, including refugees, to collective sites. A dedicated site coordination expert will lead UNHCR’s efforts in this regard.
